t: the warning mentioned in the Torah. The formula by which a man warns his wife, if he suspects her of adultery.
do not be secluded with so-and-so. Do not be alone with him in a secret place.
even if he was her father or her brother. Even if the suspected man was one of her relatives, and one might have thought a woman is generally not suspected of adultery with them.
or a gentile or a slave. Although betrothal does not take effect with them (Hilchot Ishut 4:15), and one might have thought that their relations do not count.
a shachuf... who cannot become erect. He is not capable of intercourse.
the seclusion mentioned in the Torah. The one from which a man warns his wife, and if she transgressed his words and was secluded, she is forbidden to him until she is tested.
she stayed with him long enough to become impure. They were together for a time sufficient for intercourse.
and swallow it. And gulp it down.
the bitter waters. The waters that test whether the woman was defiled, whose taste is bitter (below 3:10).

and when there are no waters of the sotah. After the Temple was destroyed, for the sotah is made to drink only by the High Court in the Temple (below 3:1); and even before that the Sanhedrin abolished the bitter waters (see below 3:19).

and she leaves without a ketubah. He divorces her without paying her ketubah money, which she forfeits if there are witnesses to ugly acts that arouse suspicion of adultery (see Hilchot Ishut 24:15, 24).
two together. He warned her against being secluded with two men together.

and likewise if no warning preceded and two came and testified... she is not forbidden to her husband. For this is not clear testimony of adultery but of seclusion only, and any seclusion not preceded by a warning does not forbid.
a minor less than nine years and a day. Whose intercourse is not considered intercourse (Hilchot Ishut 11:3; Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 1:13).
a husband who waived his warning. Gave it up and canceled it.
but after she is secluded he cannot waive. For she is already forbidden to him until she drinks.
divorced her. Before she was secluded.
he must issue another warning. If he wants to warn her, for the first warning is void.
and he must divorce her and pay the ketubah. For he has no witnesses to prove his claim.
for he cannot make her drink on his own word. On his own testimony; rather two valid witnesses to the seclusion are needed, and so she is forbidden to him forever.
they whisper about her. They say she committed adultery.

among the women who spin by the light of the moon. The talk spread until the women who gather together to spin at night talk about her conduct, but there are not two witnesses that she was secluded with that man.
to keep her. To live with her.
that she was secluded with him. With the one against whom he warned.

if he believes him... he divorces her and pays the ketubah. A single witness is not believed to make her forfeit her ketubah, and she is forbidden only because the husband's mind relies on the witness (for a similar law see Hilchot Ishut 24:17). And even if his mind relies on him, he cannot make her drink without two witnesses (as above halachah 8).
that the court warns them. The court warns in the husband's place and cautions the woman not to be secluded with a particular man.
one whose husband became deaf, etc.. All of these are unable to warn on their own, and the court acts as the husband's agents.

not to make her drink but to disqualify her from her ketubah. The court's warning does not suffice to make the woman drink and be tested, but only that she forfeits her ketubah because she behaved immodestly.
and they tear up her ketubah. She has forfeited her rights, and they tear it up as with a document that cannot be collected (Hilchot Malveh VeLoveh 23:14).
she drank the bitter waters and was cleared by them. It was proven through the waters that she was not defiled (see below 3:21).
and he again warned her about the man by whom he had made her drink. He again suspected his wife of adultery with the same man.
he does not make her drink... and she leaves without a ketubah. It stands to reason that she committed adultery with that man (Ohr Sameach; compare below halachah 13).
he made her drink. And she was found pure.
and the other warned her. The second husband.

and we do not say that surely she has been presumed, etc.. Although all her husbands suspect her regarding the same man, we do not assume that she surely committed adultery with him, and she is not forbidden without a witness.

she is forbidden to her husband forever and does not drink. She is forbidden because her husband already warned her and she was secluded, but she cannot drink and be tested because of the witness who says she was had.

as it is said, "and there is no witness against her," and here there is a witness. Only if there is no witness does she drink; this implies that any testimony, even if not acceptable elsewhere, suffices here, as below.
even a woman, a slave, or a maidservant. Those disqualified from testimony by Torah law (Hilchot Edut 9:1).
and one disqualified to testify about a transgression by rabbinic law. One disqualified from testimony by a rabbinic enactment (see ibid. 10:3-4).
a relative. A relative who is disqualified from testifying (ibid. 9:1).

the five women who hate one another. Her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, her co-wife, her sister-in-law, and her husband's daughter, who are presumed to hate her (Hilchot Gerushin 12:16).

and she is believed about her to forbid her... but not to disqualify her from her ketubah. They are not believed regarding her because they hate her, but in matters of impurity we take their words into account because there is a basis for the matter, since he had warned her previously.
as we have explained. Above halachah 14.

for one witness to the impurity of a sotah is like two, etc.. Because the first witness is believed as two, no other witness can contradict him (for similar laws see Hilchot Gerushin 12:18-23, Hilchot Rotzeach 9:13-17).
both came together. The two witnesses came together, in which case the witness to impurity was not given the credibility of two to begin with.
and two came after him. Even after his testimony had been accepted.
she drinks. For the witnesses are equal and contradict one another, and there is no witness to impurity here.
they are half and half. Equal in the force of their testimony.
we follow the majority. They decide her case by the majority of witnesses.
as we have explained. Above halachah 14.
yes. Indeed.
and she does not drink. Because the waters come to resolve a doubt.

"I am not defiled and I will not drink," etc.. She did not admit to adultery but refuses to drink and be tested (and see further below 4:3), and she forfeits her ketubah because she caused her prohibition to remain.

her husband had relations with her after she was secluded. For once she was secluded she became forbidden to him (above 1:2); and since her husband had relations with her in violation of the prohibition, the waters do not test her (below halachah 8).
and she collects her ketubah. Because the husband caused her not to drink (and see below halachah 8).
a betrothed woman. Who was betrothed to him but they have not yet come to marriage and shared life.
and a woman awaiting yibbum. A woman whose husband died without children and who waits for his brother (the yavam) to marry her or perform chalitzah, and her yavam warned her.
a minor... a minor. For their definitions see Hilchot Ishut 2:1, 10.
an androgynos. One who has both male and female sexual organs (Hilchot Ishut 2:24).
the blind. Blind.
the lame. One with a defect in his leg that causes him to limp.
the mute. One who does not speak.
and one whose hand was cut off. The palm of the hand.
who is not under her husband. Both have not yet married a husband, and are not included in "under him" (and see below 4:17).
withered. Paralyzed.
to take hold of it. To grasp it.
and even one hand of hers. Even if only one of her hands is cut off or paralyzed, she cannot drink.
a woman under her husband, etc.. For this equates their situations.
a minor whose father married her off. Whose betrothal is by Torah law (Hilchot Ishut 3:11).
she is forbidden to her husband. Like any woman who committed adultery willingly (Hilchot Gerushin 11:14; for a minor who committed adultery see also Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 3:2).
as we said. Above halachah 2.

a minor who exercised refusal (ma'un). A minor who is an orphan from her father and whom her mother or brothers married off with her consent. Her betrothal is not from the Torah, and she can at any time she wishes refuse to live with her husband and leave without a get (Hilchot Ishut 4:7-8).
for she has no will to become forbidden to her husband. She is not forbidden to her husband even if she committed adultery willingly, for by Torah law she is not considered married to him.
even if he was a priest. Since she is not considered married, she is like an unmarried woman who committed adultery, who is permitted to a priest (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 18:2).
to his zekukah. To a woman awaiting yibbum.
and was secluded before her husband had relations with her. Her husband never had relations with her before she was secluded.
and the freed woman. A gentile maidservant who was freed, and who has the law of a convert. She is permitted to marry an Israelite but forbidden to a priest (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 12:17, 18:3).
and a mamzeret. A woman born of forbidden relations, who is forbidden to enter the congregation but permitted to marry a mamzer or a convert (ibid. 15:1-2, 15:7).
a saris. One who has a physical defect that prevents him from fathering children.
a saris chamah. One born a saris (for his signs see Hilchot Ishut 2:13).

a saris adam. One made a saris by man, which includes one with crushed testes and one whose organ was cut off (Hilchot Ishut 2:14, Issurei Bi'ah 16:3-9). They are forbidden to enter the congregation but permitted to marry a convert and a freed woman (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 16:1).
pregnant and nursing... and he makes her drink as she is. They do not wait until the fetus is born or the baby is weaned.
and she does not collect a ketubah. Since she was secluded after he had warned her, and there is no possibility that she drink (see above 1:2, and Hilchot Ishut 24:24).
all his days after he grew up. Throughout his adult life.

had relations with his betrothed in his father-in-law's house, who is forbidden by rabbinic law. For by rabbinic enactment a man who betrothed a woman is forbidden to have relations with her until he brings her into the wedding canopy and marries her (Hilchot Ishut 10:1).
among those liable under a prohibition or under a positive commandment. For their details see Hilchot Ishut 1:7-8.
a sheniyah. A relative forbidden by rabbinic law (see Hilchot Ishut 1:6).
she is forbidden to him on this account as well. Besides the first prohibition (prohibition, positive commandment, sheniyah), she is also forbidden to him because of the warning and the seclusion.
another's pregnant woman and another's nursing woman. The Sages decreed that she not marry, lest the fetus or the baby be harmed (Hilchot Gerushin 11:25-28).
for there is no transgression here. She is forbidden to him only because of concern for danger to the child, and she is permitted to him after a time.
one who is fit to bear children. Capable of giving birth.
an aylonit. A woman whose sexual development is defective and who does not bear children (for her signs see Hilchot Ishut 2:6).
does not drink. For this marriage is in transgression as long as he has not fulfilled the commandment to be fruitful and multiply (ibid. 15:7).

and she shall conceive seed. Said of one who drank and was found pure (see below 3:22). It does not mean a restriction that only one fit to bear children is tested, but that one fit to bear children is blessed.
with ease. Easily.
she was already fit to drink. She was fit to drink at the time of the warning, when they were permitted to each other in marriage.
the aylonit was already excluded from drinking. She was excluded from drinking at the time of the warning, and therefore she does not drink even if afterward he may keep her.
that her husband did not wish... that she did not wish. That both can refuse (above halachah 1).
that a witness to impurity came against her. Above 1:14.
or she admitted. She admitted she committed adultery (above halachah 1).
the women who are not fit to drink. Detailed above in halachah 2.
that the court warned. Detailed above 1:10.
from the tradition. The Sages' tradition.

an ugly matter, such as that they entered after him... and the like. Where it is evident there was transgression, although there is no clear testimony of adultery (Hilchot Ishut 24:15, with further examples there). In all these cases her husband may divorce her without a ketubah.
she shall not marry the one accused. The man suspected, so as not to confirm the suspicion of adultery (for a similar law see Hilchot Gerushin 10:14).
she need not leave. So that a slur will not be cast on her children, that they are mamzerim.
when the city was in an uproar. When a rumor of adultery went around the city.
and the report did not cease. The rumor continued to spread.
if there was no talk there. They did not talk about it and the rumor did not spread.
not because of fear. The rumor stopped on its own, and not out of fear of a person who wants to deny the rumor.
if she married the accused, she need not leave, etc.. It is to be assumed that it was a false rumor.

and she married another and he divorced her, she is forbidden to marry the accused, etc.. Although marriage to another voids the suspicion (see Hilchot Gerushin 10:15), she is forbidden to him from the outset because of the severity of the prohibition.
that she committed adultery with this one. With her present husband.
she must leave this one. For she is clearly forbidden to him.
and these are my witnesses. The witnesses to the warning and the seclusion.
and two Torah scholars are assigned to him to guard him. To accompany them on their way to Jerusalem.
she became forbidden to him until she drinks. And if he has relations with her, the waters will not test her (above 2:8; for the prohibition see Hilchot Gerushin 11:14).
for only the High Court makes the sotah drink. Hilchot Sanhedrin 5:1.
not in front of her husband. So that she will not be ashamed to admit her act.
much wine does, etc.. All of these can draw one to adultery.
much youth does. Young age, which has playfulness and light-mindedness.
for the great Name that was written in holiness. The explicit Name, which it is forbidden to erase (Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 6:1-2).
to be erased into the water. To be erased in water.
and were swept away. Were carried away by their evil inclination.
great and precious. Important and honored.
and they tell her the story of Judah, etc.. All of these stumbled in forbidden relations (see Genesis 38, ibid. 35:22, II Samuel 13:1-22).
and the story of Reuben with his father's concubine according to its plain sense. For according to the plain sense Reuben lay with Bilhah, Jacob's concubine (and see Hilchot Tefillah 12:12).
she stood by her statement. She continued to claim that she is pure.
to the eastern gate of the Temple court. The main gate of the courtyard around the Temple, also called the Nicanor Gate (Hilchot Beit HaBechirah 5:5).
and they take her up from place to place... until her soul grows weary. They lead her about the Temple to exhaust her, so that she will admit the truth.
opposite the eastern gate, outside. Outside the Temple court (see Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 4:2).
if she was dressed in white, they dress her in black. If the woman was wearing white garments, they clothe her in black garments, which are garments of disgrace (see Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 6:11).
and they remove gold and silver jewelry. They take off her ornaments, so that she will be disgraced. [Note: In the Commentary to the Mishnah, Rambam writes and vocalizes the word noy as no'i.]
and they gather. Collect.
and all the women will be chastised, etc.. They will be disciplined and will learn not to do so.
a shawl. A garment that covers her head and body.
and the kuppach on her head. A cap, a head covering (see Hilchot Ishut 24:11-13).
and her mind is settled with them. She feels secure in their presence, and she is strengthened and does not admit.
in a language she recognizes. In a language she understands, not necessarily the language of the Torah.
be cleared of these bitter, cursing waters. Drink the waters and nothing will happen to you, and so you will prove that you are clean of sin.
swells. Swells up.
amen. Since she answered amen to the oath, it is as if she swore herself (Hilchot Nedarim 2:1, Hilchot Shevuot 2:1).

and he informs her that the belly will swell, etc.. Because the order in the language of the oath is reversed, the priest informs her what will actually happen, so that she will not think the action of the waters is out of order.
of pure hide. Of a pure animal (Hilchot Tefillin 1:10).

with ink that has no kalkantos. Kalkantos is copper oxide, which fixes the ink so that it will not be erased. In the scroll of the sotah the writing must be erasable with water (see also below halachah 10, 4:9).
for the sake of the woman, like a get. The scroll must be written only for that particular sotah, like a get (see Hilchot Gerushin chapter 2).
and he writes the Name as it is written. When he reaches the name of God, he writes it as it is written in the Torah (with the letters yod, heh, vav, heh) and not as it is pronounced ("Adonai").
an earthenware vessel in which no work was done, etc.. A new vessel must be used (for a similar law see Hilchot Tumat Tzara'at 11:1).
worn. Worn out and old.
he returned it to the kiln until it was renewed. He put it again in the oven in which earthenware vessels are fired, until it was burned and became like new.
and in a half-log that was in the Temple. There was a special measuring vessel that held exactly half a log (Hilchot Kelei HaMikdash 1:17).
and there was a place there. In the floor of the Sanctuary.
a tablet. A board.
the Tabernacle. The Temple.
wormwood. A bitter plant.
and he erases the scroll into them for her sake. The scroll is erased for the sake of that woman (as above halachah 8).
on her clothes opposite her face. In front.
he uncovers her heart. He bares her chest.
and loosens the braids of her hair. He undoes the braids of her hair.
to disgrace her. To make her ugly and shame her.
the practice of Egypt. Of those steeped in adultery (see Leviticus 18:3).
and ties it above her breasts. He ties the garments with it above her breasts.
an issaron. A tenth of an ephah.
in an Egyptian basket. A basket woven of palm leaves.

from the remainder of the chamber. From public funds, from what was given in the half-shekel contribution for buying the Temple's offerings and was left over for other Temple needs (Hilchot Shekalim 2:4).
and he places it in her hands to tire her. The priest puts the basket with the offering into the woman's hands so that she carries it herself and grows tired, as above halachah 3.
in a service vessel. Vessels used for holy service in the Temple.
and he does not put oil on it, etc.. Unlike an ordinary meal offering, to which oil and frankincense are added (Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 12:7).
and if he put. And offered it on the altar (ibid. halachah 8).
and the whole time that he uncovered her head and put the issaron, etc.. During the time that the priest uncovers her hair and places the offering in her hands (above halachot 11-12).
and waves it. He lifts the offering with her.
he moves it forward and back, up and down. He extends the offering away from himself and brings it back, raises it and lowers it (see Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 9:6-7).
he brings it near... like the other meal offerings of an individual. He brings the vessel containing the offering near and touches it to a corner of the altar (ibid. 12:6).
and takes a handful and burns the handful. He takes a portion of the offering in his palm (ibid. 13:13) and offers it on the altar.
and the remainder is eaten by the priests. As with the remainder of every meal offering (ibid. 12:9).
her face turns pale. Turns greenish.
and she fills with veins. Her blood vessels swell and stand out from the flesh.

and they say, "Take her out, take her out," lest she spread her impurity, etc.. The priests urge that she be taken out of the Temple court, lest she see blood and become impure, and she may not be there in her impurity (Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 3:3).
swells. Swells up.
because of him. On his account.
as we have explained. Above 2:8.
and if he transgressed. The one who had a forbidden union.

and they relied on the verse in the Prophets, etc.. When the Sanhedrin abolished the test by the bitter waters, they relied on the words of rebuke in the books of the Prophets, that with the multiplication of adultery God no longer punishes adulterous women.
even though she is not commanded in the study of Torah. For a woman is obligated neither to learn nor to teach (Hilchot Talmud Torah 1:1).
it suspends it for her and she does not die at once. The delivery of her punishment is delayed because of her merit; it hangs pending, and she does not die immediately.
wastes away. Weakens.

even if he was a priest. For his wife is forbidden to him even if she committed adultery under duress, and one might have thought the waters do not test her (Commentary to the Mishnah, Sotah 4:4; Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 18:6; below halachah 24).
and even if they began... she is permitted. Because these are not certain signs that she committed adultery.
they illuminate. They light up.
and if she had an illness, it will pass. She will be healed of it.
to give birth with difficulty. To give birth in great pain.
witnesses to impurity. Who testify that she committed adultery.

that he had relations with her... in the manner of limbs. That he lay with her and rubbed against her other organs, but did not have relations with her in a way considered intercourse (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 1:10).

the court turns to the needs of the public. At this time the courts would attend to matters not dealt with during the winter months (for similar matters see Hilchot Kilayim 2:15, Hilchot Arachin VaCharamin 8:1, Hilchot Rotzeach 8:6).
and over one fit to be warned. A woman for whom the court warns in place of the husband (see above 1:10).
she may. She is permitted.
and she is neither afraid nor frightened. It is reasonable to assume that she refused to drink because she admitted her guilt.
and it is not fit to make another sotah drink with it. Because the scroll must be written for her sake (above 3:8).
is scattered on the ashes. The place where the altar's ashes are put, east of the ramp (Hilchot Temidin UMusafin 2:12).
they make her gurgle. They make her swallow the water into her throat.
stand on your feet. Stand steadily and without fear.
as medicine. As a remedy.
she said, "I am defiled". And did not say, "I will not drink."
the water is poured out, because it has no holiness. There is no need to store it away or treat it with honor.
as her offering is by day. For all offerings are brought only by day (Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 4:1).
out of order. Not in sequence.
he wrote it as a letter. Without ruling the lines (see Hilchot Sefer Torah 7:4).
two columns. Two columns.
the diftera. Hide that is not processed all the way.
with komos. A dye made from resin.
to be erased. To be erased.
not for her sake. For the sake of the sotah (see above 3:8).
and he again divided them... and if he made her drink, it is valid. For it may be that he divided them properly.
he should not make her drink the rest. For ideally she must drink all the waters.
our sotah waters. Over which a night passed without her being made to drink from them.
are disqualified by being left overnight. Like anything sanctified in a service vessel over which a night has passed (Hilchot Beit HaBechirah 3:18).
rakbuvit. Something rotted and crumbled.
with an axe. A digging tool.
which is in the ground of the Tabernacle. It is lying in the ground and there is no need to dig it up.
if her offering became impure... it is redeemed, etc.. Its holiness must be redeemed for money of its value, and it is given to the Temple treasury.
after he sanctified it in a service vessel. And it can no longer be redeemed (Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach 6:4-5).
and likewise if she said... or she died. In all of these they do not make her drink (above 1:14, 2:1, 2:7).
before the offering is taken by the handful. Before a handful is taken from it to be offered on the altar.
witnesses to impurity. Two witnesses that she committed adultery.
the remainder is not eaten. What is left of the offering after the handful was taken for offering, which is normally eaten by the priests (Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 12:9), is not eaten here.

the remainder of her offering is not eaten because the husband has a share in it. For the offering is acquired with his money, and a priest's offering is not eaten but is entirely burned (Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 12:9, 12:12).
for the fire offerings. For the altar fire.
because she has a share in it. For the offering comes to atone for her.

her witnesses were found to be zomemim. The witnesses to the seclusion were found to be false witnesses, when witnesses came and testified that they were with them at the time of the event in another place.
her offering goes out to common use. Because it was sanctified in error (see Hilchot Arachin VaCharamin 6:34).
on account of. Because of.
the husband may. The husband is permitted.
to extend the oath over her. When she swears, the husband can add to her oath further oaths on the same matter.
he married his yevamah. He married his deceased brother's wife, who died childless.
when she was awaiting yibbum. When she was designated for yibbum. If she committed adultery, she is not forbidden to him (Hilchot Yibbum VeChalitzah 2:20).
she is forbidden to him. For she was forbidden to her husband (ibid. 6:19).
for the future. Regarding the future.
under him. While they are married.

therefore, when she commits adultery in the future, the water tests her and those events befall her. The water she drinks now will affect her and test her when she commits adultery, and then the ailments described above in 3:16 will cling to her.
therefore it says, "amen, amen". The doubled "amen" teaches the multiplicity of oaths with which she can be made to swear.
to warn their wives. To caution them when there is suspicion of adultery.
to jump and warn before witnesses at the outset. To begin with a warning that may forbid her to him, without first cautioning her.
and he inspects their ways. He checks and examines their conduct.
your tent... your abode. Terms for a person's home, meaning his wife and family.
